description: Team Orbit-X (Cairo) presents a Space Mission Design 3D web app using Three.js and NASA data. It features a holographic Sci-Fi UI, core explosions, time-travel timelines, gravity simulations, base locators, and an AI Mission Advisor for physics feedback.
summary:
ORBIT-X is an interactive 3D web platform that transforms complex space science data into an immersive space exploration and mission design experience.

Our team developed a platform where users can explore ten celestial bodies, investigate planetary internal structures, travel back approximately 3.5 billion years to discover ancient Mars, assess potential landing sites, and simulate gravitational differences across different worlds.

ORBIT-X combines React, TypeScript, and Three.js to deliver interactive 3D experiences, alongside Google's Gemini API, which powers Commander X, an AI-driven mission assistant.

One of our most innovative features is the 4-Way Pyramid Hologram, which transforms four synchronized mobile screen views into a holographic-style planetary visualization.

By combining scientific information, artificial intelligence, interactive simulations, and immersive visualization, ORBIT-X makes space science more accessible and engaging. Our mission is to inspire curiosity, encourage scientific thinking, and help students experience space exploration beyond traditional learning methods.
details:
ORBIT-X – Project Details

1. What Does ORBIT-X Do and How Does It Work?

ORBIT-X is an interactive 3D web platform designed to transform complex space science concepts into an immersive space exploration and mission design experience.

The platform allows users to explore ten celestial bodies through interactive 3D models, investigate planetary structures, travel through the geological history of Mars, evaluate potential landing locations, and simulate gravitational differences across celestial bodies.

Users can interact with several integrated modules:

  • Explode Core: Explore the internal structures of celestial bodies, including their crust, mantle, and core.
  • Cosmic Time Machine: Travel approximately 3.5 billion years into Mars' past to discover its ancient environment and evidence of flowing water.
  • Mission Viability Assessment: Investigate potential landing locations using coordinates and environmental factors such as radiation and terrain conditions.
  • Gravity Simulator: Compare gravitational forces and calculate theoretical jumping heights on different celestial bodies.
  • Commander X: Interact with an AI-powered mission assistant that explains scientific concepts and guides users through the platform.
  • 4-Way Pyramid Hologram: Experience a synchronized four-view display that creates a floating 3D holographic-style visualization of celestial bodies when viewed through a transparent pyramid.

2. What Are Its Benefits?

ORBIT-X makes space science more accessible by converting complex scientific information into interactive visual experiences.

Its main benefits include:

  • Making planetary science easier to understand through 3D exploration.
  • Encouraging hands-on learning instead of passive reading.
  • Helping students understand planetary environments and mission-planning challenges.
  • Demonstrating how gravity and environmental conditions differ across celestial bodies.
  • Introducing users to the role of scientific data and AI in modern space exploration.
  • Combining education, experimentation, and interactive technology in one platform.

3. What Is the Expected Impact?

Our goal is to make space exploration more understandable, engaging, and accessible, especially for students and beginners interested in astronomy, physics, and space technology.

ORBIT-X encourages curiosity, critical thinking, scientific investigation, and problem-solving.

By connecting real scientific concepts with interactive simulations, the platform aims to inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts, researchers, and engineers.

It also demonstrates how digital technologies can transform complex NASA-related scientific information into meaningful educational experiences.

4. What Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware, and Software Were Used?

ORBIT-X was developed as an interactive web-based platform using modern web technologies, real-time 3D visualization, and artificial intelligence integration.

Technology Stack:

  • Frontend Framework: React – Used to build the interactive user interface and platform components.
  • Programming Language: TypeScript – Used to develop structured, maintainable, and type-safe application logic.
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js – Used to create and render interactive 3D celestial bodies and immersive planetary exploration experiences.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini API – Integrated to power Commander X, the AI-powered mission assistant that helps users understand scientific concepts and navigate the platform.
  • Scientific References: NASA and NASA JPL resources – Used as references for planetary science and space-related information.
  • Development Environment: Web-based development environment for building, testing, and improving the platform.
  • Hardware: Computers for development and compatible mobile devices for testing the responsive interface and 4-way pyramid holographic display.

These technologies work together to deliver an interactive experience that combines scientific exploration, 3D visualization, and AI-powered assistance.

5. What Makes ORBIT-X Creative and Innovative?

The creativity of ORBIT-X comes from combining several different space exploration experiences into one interactive platform.

Instead of presenting planets through ordinary images and text, ORBIT-X allows users to explore their structures, investigate their history, simulate physical conditions, and participate in mission-planning activities.

One of its most distinctive innovations is the 4-Way Pyramid Hologram, which transforms a mobile screen into four synchronized views to create a holographic-style planetary visualization using a transparent pyramid.

Another innovative aspect is the integration of Commander X, which combines AI-assisted guidance with interactive scientific exploration.

The platform brings together education, visualization, simulation, and experimentation in a unified experience.

6. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

During the development of ORBIT-X, our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Accuracy: Using reliable scientific references and maintaining consistency with established planetary science information.
  • Educational Accessibility: Making complex scientific concepts understandable for students and beginners.
  • User Experience: Creating an intuitive and interactive interface that encourages exploration.
  • Performance: Considering the computational requirements of 3D visualization and interactive simulations.
  • Innovation: Developing distinctive experiences that go beyond traditional educational websites.
  • Practicality: Designing features that users can access through standard web browsers and compatible mobile devices.
  • Scalability: Building a concept that can be expanded with additional celestial bodies, scientific datasets, and mission-planning capabilities.

Conclusion

ORBIT-X is more than a platform for viewing planets. It is an interactive gateway to understanding the science, challenges, and possibilities of space exploration.

By combining 3D visualization, scientific information, artificial intelligence, physical simulations, and an innovative holographic experience, ORBIT-X transforms learning about space into an engaging journey of discovery.

ORBIT-X – Your Mission. Your Universe. Your Discovery.
